name: input.mouse.drag
description: Press a mouse button at the current cursor position, smoothly move to (x, y) over `steps` interpolated positions, and release. Atomic: a single SendInput batch where possible, ensuring continuous-movement detection by the OS. Per issue #68.

x.description: Target X (absolute virtual-screen) for the release position.

y.description: Target Y (absolute) for the release position.

button.description: Mouse button to hold during the drag.

steps.description: Number of intermediate move events emitted between the down and up. Linear interpolation from the starting position to (x, y). Each move is a separate INPUT_MOUSE event in the same SendInput batch. Higher values = smoother visible drag and more reliable drag-detection on slow-press-detection-sensitive targets; lower values = faster. The OS drag threshold is `GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXDRAG)` / `SM_CYDRAG` (~4 px); 10 steps over typical drag distances clears it comfortably.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. The cursor ends at (x, y) (or the clamped equivalent if off-screen).

x-implementations.name: send_input_batch
x-implementations.description: Single Win32 `SendInput` call carrying [button-down, N×MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE | MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE | MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK, button-up] in one batch. Single call ensures the OS sees the event sequence without interleaving from real input. NT 5+.

x-implementations.name: mouse_event_sequence
x-implementations.description: Win32 `mouse_event` sequential calls for NT 4 / 9x where SendInput is unavailable. The lack of batching means real user input can interleave; rare on automation-only machines but possible. Agent issues calls in tight loop with no Sleep between.

windows-modern.description: Single SendInput batch: down + N interpolated MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE events + up. The MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK flag ensures coordinates work across multi-monitor setups. UIPI may silently drop drags directed at higher-IL windows; the down-event's UIPI check is the authoritative signal — failures return ERR uipi_blocked. The drag does NOT enter the agent's per-connection held-input set (it's atomic — the up event always fires before the verb returns).

windows-classic.description: SendInput batch on NT 5+; sequential mouse_event calls on NT 4 / 9x. NT 4 is single-monitor only — multi-monitor coords clamp to the primary monitor. No UIPI on classic, so drags cross all process boundaries freely.
